profile.headline: Java/Android Developer
profile.summary:
I've more than 15 years of working experience from backend to frontend, embedded and mobile development. My favorite things are Algorithms, problem solving and Optimization. I like a great place to work with a nice environment and awesome co-workers, were i can learn new things from them and share the knowledge i've learn over the years.

Having knowledge of different platform and/or systems has help me in understanding how things work and how certain problems are solved there so that i can use that on other places that might be useful as well.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
- Server-Driven UI (Mosaic): Developed and maintained out Server-Driven UI framework enabling product and feature teams to iterate rapidly and ship UI updates dynamically without requiring client-side app updates or app store approvals.

-CI & Build Infrastructure: I'm part of out continuous integration reliability and build stability initiatives; led JDK version migrations, diagnosed and eliminated flaky tests, and overall system reliability across client builds.

-Performance Tooling & Observability: Engineered custom performance monitoring libraries and diagnostic tools to track critical app metrics, isolate performance regressions, and address systemic bottlenecks.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
I work on the android performance tooling team:
- I found that our production tracing had been not working properly for the past several years, and our data had been polluted due some api usage mistakes. Found the problem which was causing this and started a big migration in all of our codebase to fix this. After that we now get the proper duration of our spans and we can trust the data that comes from those traces from production.

- Improved our tracing infrastructure
    - Added common activity / fragment lifecycles in a way that allow us to measure the whole duration of this callbacks and prevents developers from putting code outside the manually measured spans.
    - Added markers for important things like configuration changes, multi window mode, PiP, view inflations, etc...

- I found out that our app supported split screen and the experience was not the best during this mode, it turned out a bigger than expected amount of daily users use our app in this mode (almost 2%). So I started a conversation with higher ups to invest some time to fix this, due to our lack of developer free cycles this was eventually not done.

- I found a problem in Google play store delivery that was causing 3% of our production crashes, this was related to the play store not delivery all the required XMLs for our app to function properly, so it would crash before we even had time to do any code execution (before onBaseContextAttach). This problem was reported to Google and they found the cause and fix it, fixing all those crashes at the same time.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Android developer on client infra for Google Meet,

- Change part of our infra to a partial update whenever the participant's list changed, before we used to update everything whenever anything in one participant changed. This was to allow us to support bigger meeting sizes in the future, as the current situation would had made it impossible.

- Updated our internal annotations processor to allow Dagger module creations with a single annotation on the implementation class. The result of this was easy to use API that made sure the generated code was always correct and we only loaded and executed the code that was necessary. Preventing experiments to be restarted due to wrong configuration.

- Helped with the migration to Android U before it's public beta release, and provided changes needed for the android api, some of which had to be implemented on Android V as it was too late to changed them.
positions.insights: Skills: Java · Android · Software Development · Kotlin

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description:
Worked on the Facebook for android Startup performance team. My team manage CPU, memory, resources and everything been used during the start of the application.

- Wrote a Buck plugin that would read all the layouts that were specified in the allowed list in the modules, and it would generate Java code and package that in our APK instead of the XMLs. This made our customer's experience better and faster by allowing us to do the following:
    - Prevented lock contention with other threads as we didn't read the xml resource when inflating
    - Prevented conflicts with other threads while reading resources, as some of them would get inlined
    - Enforced valid xml properties at compile time
    - Avoided reflection during inflation
    - Allowed us to decide how resources were loaded and in which thread that happened, instead of blocking by default the main thread whenever a resource had to be read.

- Found and issue were we were not packaging in out APK some of the resources used on the startup, which resulted in network calls during our critical paths of our app. This made our customer's experience worst, as it was delaying our startups by a considerable amount of time, plus it was wasting networks resources every time they started the app.

- Optimized the Top bar in the Facebook app as it was bloated after many years of experiments on top of experiments, the code was able to be cut by a substantial amount (around 80% of the code) and the layout was simplified to improve our inflation time. Also test were written to make sure we didn't break LTR/RTL or different screen sizes as it had happened in the past. On top of that, the p50 startup time saw a nice double digit milliseconds decrease as this was a considerable portion of the startup path.

positions.title: Software Engineer II
positions.description:
Android Wear work:
- Only developer on bringing our OneNote app into android wear
- This was the first keyboard that existed in Android Wear
- Added plumbing into the Android OneNote native codebase to communicate with the wear app
- Wrote the Outlook Watch Face, which allowed you a bird's eye view of how your day was going to be and allowed you to see the content in your meetings if you which to do so
- Modified the Android Outlook codebase to allow for communication with the wear app

Other work:
- Wrote a Gradle plugin that would go ahead and optimize our pngs when compiling our app, it would avoid to optimize already optimized pngs.
- Work with other team mates to improve the infrastructure of the Microsoft translator app for Android


Microsoft Teams:
- 6th developer on this project before it went public
- Started our modularization work, as we used to have 1 single module with all the code in it
- Wrote a few annotation processors to simplify our codebase and remove repetitive patterns
- Modified our Giphy interaction to allow it to be used under 2G network connections
- Improved performance of certain parts of our apps
- Introduced ConstraintLayout in our code base, which allowed before impossible layouts to be built, including the "bubbles" in our chat page.
- Found issues in how we generated our SVGs, which was causing bloated SVGs with thousands of commands, as when zoomed in you could see lines weren't straight and curves were oddly shaped in some areas. Worked with designers to improve our exporting flow and fix this problem for future releases
